<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via ObjectSchemaBase (symbol, a top-level const object))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9b3227fe235beffbca5b22370af827a4a016deef` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ddeda5ef4b8b7b09076a704efcd556854e1cf0ee` — the merge of head `0fbfc45244563d5a4acd2e68cf48599b3ca83c3a` into base `9b3227fe235beffbca5b22370af827a4a016deef`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ddeda5ef4b8b7b09076a704efcd556854e1cf0ee && git checkout ddeda5ef4b8b7b09076a704efcd556854e1cf0ee
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9b3227fe235beffbca5b22370af827a4a016deef 0fbfc45244563d5a4acd2e68cf48599b3ca83c3a && git checkout -B drift-repro 9b3227fe235beffbca5b22370af827a4a016deef && git merge --no-ff 0fbfc45244563d5a4acd2e68cf48599b3ca83c3a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9b3227fe235beffbca5b22370af827a4a016deef
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9b3227fe235beffbca5b22370af827a4a016deef` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review brief — PR #36012 @ `834205699cf0979a6652aa3bc2de8137b8125c52` (card #35985)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts packages/spec/src/data/index.ts packages/spec/src/data/object-icon.ts packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #35985: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #36012: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `834205699cf0979a6652aa3bc2de8137b8125c52`
  · the check-runs on `834205699cf0979a6652aa3bc2de8137b8125c52`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/index.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object-icon.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/3d3cbaf6-4903-5fed-92d4-c2b94a45e868/scratchpad/pr-36012/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## 席位核对 — REWORK (text only) (L1-b)

Head-sha: 834205699cf0979a6652aa3bc2de8137b8125c52 · read 2026-11-21T07:48Z

### 维护者速读

- 内容本身可以合：
  - 对象可以从 9 种固定颜色里选一种。侧栏、应用首页菜单和手机菜单里的对象改成「彩色圆角方块 + 白色图标」，没设颜色的显示灰色。
  - 设计器里选图标时可以一起选颜色。
  - AI 生成方案时也会给每个对象配不同的颜色。
  - 不能填任意色值，所以每种颜色在浅色和深色主题下都清楚可辨。
- 要返工的只有发版记录：`@objectstack/platform-objects` 这个包的 10 种语言表单文字（新增的「颜色」一栏）改了，但发版说明里没列这个包，发版时它不会带上新版本号。补一行就行，代码不用改。
- 列表头、记录头、搜索等其他位置的图标在第 2 个 PR 改，AI 说明文字在第 3 个 PR 改。

### Must-fix

- **M1 — the changeset misses `@objectstack/platform-objects`.** This diff changes 13 files in that published package. The 10 `*.metadata-forms.generated.ts` packs ship the new `color` row's label and help text, so consumers get new form text with no version bump. The other two files there are the count pins. Add `'@objectstack/platform-objects': minor` (it ships a new row of an `added` key, matching spec's level), with one sentence on what it ships. l1-face flags it. The `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` flag is test-only (the property-count pin), so it needs no entry.

### Should-fix

None.

### Nits (optional)

- N1: the `object-icon.ts` header still says the leaf "does not join the package's published exports". That was true of `OBJECT_ICON_SCHEMA`, but `OBJECT_COLORS` / `ObjectColor` are now exported from `@objectstack/spec/data` (the changeset says so). Add one line saying which names are exported.
- N2: `NavigationRenderer` (published `@object-ui/layout`) now draws every `object` entry as a tile, even for a host that passes no `resolveTargetColor`. Such a host gets gray tiles where it had line icons. The changeset's "Navigation draws objects as tiles" covers it, and the bump is minor. Naming the no-resolver case (gray) in that bullet would tell other hosts what they will see.

### Checked

- l1-face at `83420569`: one flag (M1 above). Otherwise:
  - CI is complete at this head: 61 success, 9 expected skip, 0 failed, mergeable clean.
  - `Part of #35985` is right: there are two more PRs.
  - The declarations read `Clause-②: yes (widening)` · `Metadata-protocol: added`, and spec/components/layout/app-shell/i18n are at minor.
  - `Skills-docs: follow-up` points to PR 3.
- Spec:
  - `OBJECT_COLOR_SCHEMA` is a closed `z.enum` of nine names, optional, and declared once beside `icon`.
  - `ObjectSchema` and `BlueprintObjectSchema` share the leaf. The strict mirror uses `.unwrap().nullable()`, the same pattern as `icon`.
  - `#ff0000` is refused and the refusal lists the names (pinned).
  - The FLS reference table classifies `color: keep`.
  - The liveness entry is `live`, with in-repo evidence for both a reader (navigation) and a writer (inspector).
  - The generated references and baselines (api-surface, authorable-surface, export-origins, state-counts) moved with it, and their gates are green.
- Form row: the 10 locale packs carry real text (read zh-CN), and the two echo-decision count pins are updated. That is the usual cost of a new form row.
- `ObjectIconTile`: static palette utilities with explicit `dark:` variants, no inline colour (the styling rule holds). White on each square is ≥3:1, which is right for a glyph (non-text contrast), and it is pinned for both themes. `objectColorOrDefault` maps anything off-palette to gray. `aria-hidden` applies unless a title is given.
- Navigation: the sidebar, the app-home menu and the phone menu use one tile for object entries. Dashboards, pages and links keep line icons. `useNavTargetColor` reads the colour from the same metadata cache `useNavTargetIcon` reads, so there is no new request.
- The blueprint's applier sits outside this repo. Carrying `color` into the built object there is the opening PR 3 names, so nothing in-repo drops it.

### Owed

- A text-only head for M1. I'll read only the changeset delta.
- Fable L2 is the seat's. This L1 does not replace it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `834205699cf0979a6652aa3bc2de8137b8125c52`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/index.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object-icon.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts + ui/packages/components/src/custom/object-icon-tile.tsx, ui/packages/components/src/custom/index.ts, ui/packages/layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useNavTargetIcon.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/UnifiedSidebar.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/nav-menu-renderer.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/color-variant-field.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ObjectDefaultInspector.tsx, packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts, packages/spec/liveness/object.json

Inputs read: card #35985 (body, triage comment, claim comment; no ruling and no earlier record on it), the PR body, the 50-file list, the net diff `origin/main...pr-36012` at the head above, and the head's check-runs. Every check-run that ran concluded `success` (Test Core 10/10, Test UI 16/16, both type checks, Lint and repo gates, Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Build Docs, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate); the rest are `skipped` opt-in or schedule jobs. Nothing was built or run locally. The rest of the diff (tests, generated translations and baselines, docs reference pages, i18n bundles, the changeset prose) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- `ObjectSchema.color` (new optional key, `z.enum` over nine names). RIGHT, and a pure widening: `ObjectSchemaBase` is a `strictObject`, so `color` on an object was refused as an unknown key on `main`; no document that parsed before is refused now, and no document changes meaning (absent stays absent, no default is written). There is no `color` entry in the object unknown-key guidance or alias table to collide with.
- Refusal of an off-palette value (`#ff0000`, `Blue`, `success`, `default`, empty string) at path `color`, message listing the nine names. RIGHT; it is the card's third acceptance line and is what a closed enum gives. Pinned by `object-color.test.ts`, green in Test Core.
- `BlueprintObjectSchema.color` (lenient, optional): the same leaf by identity. RIGHT, a widening: the lenient object is a plain `z.object`, so a `color` there was dropped silently before and is now carried or refused at `objects[i].color`. A blueprint that carried a junk `color` and parsed before is refused now; that set is empty in practice for the generated path, because the strict mirror could not emit the key at all, and the same was true of `icon` in #32890.
- `SolutionBlueprintStrictSchema.objects[].color` (required, nullable). RIGHT as a mirror key. It does tighten the strict accept set (a strict object without `color` parsed on `main` and is refused here, and the exported `SolutionBlueprintStrict` input type gains a required property). The repo's standing reading of that is `yes (widening)` with a one-line note for hand producers (#24152, #24213, #30484, #30655, #34287); only #32890 called it breaking, and that changeset was narrowing on another count. The strict schema is only the `generateObject` output contract; stored and applied blueprints go through the lenient schema. See nit N3 for the missing producer sentence.
- New public exports from `@objectstack/spec/data`: `OBJECT_COLORS` (const) and `ObjectColor` (type). RIGHT; `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` carry both, and the two leaves (`OBJECT_ICON_SCHEMA`, `OBJECT_COLOR_SCHEMA`) stay out of the barrel as the `index.ts` comment says.
- Authorable surface: `data/Object:color` and `ai/BlueprintObject:color` added, object card count 50 to 51, liveness `object` 84 to 85 live. RIGHT, all consistent with one new key.
- `object.form.ts` gains the `color` row. RIGHT; required by the form and zod reconciliation, and it changes no accept set.
- `OBJECT_REFERENCE_POSITIONS.color: keep` in `metadata-core`. RIGHT: a palette name names no field, so the FLS scrub has nothing to remove.
- New public surface in the UI packages: `ObjectIconTile`, `OBJECT_COLOR_TILE_CLASS`, `objectColorOrDefault`, `ObjectIconTileProps`, `ObjectIconTileSize` from `@object-ui/components`; `NavTargetColorResolver` and the optional `resolveTargetColor` prop on `NavigationRenderer`; `useNavTargetColor`; the optional `tileColor` / `onTileColorChange` on `IconPickerWidget`. RIGHT, all additive and optional. One behaviour change rides with them and is declared in the PR body: every `object` navigation entry is drawn as a tile, gray when no resolver or no colour answers, in every `NavigationRenderer` host.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening). The PR body and the changeset both carry it, with `Metadata-protocol: added`, and they agree with the diff: a new authorable key is `added`, and `added` takes at least `minor` on the packages it moves. The changeset gives `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@object-ui/components`, `@object-ui/layout`, `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/i18n` minor, and `@objectstack/metadata-core` patch. That matches what publishes: new exports and a new key in spec, new exports in components and layout, new props and a hook in app-shell, new keys in i18n, one table row in metadata-core. Nothing is removed, renamed or tombstoned, so no ADR-0087 disposition and no migration entry are owed. `Check Changeset` and the PR-body guards are green on the head.

Two remarks, neither changes the level: `@objectstack/platform-objects` ships the regenerated form translations and is not listed, but it sits in the fixed group with `@objectstack/spec` and takes the minor with it (earlier changesets are mixed on listing it); and nit N3 below.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Claim flag 1, "liveness needs a live reader, so PR 1 also switches the shared navigation path": ANSWERED, holds. `liveness/object.json` anchors `color` on `NavigationItemRenderer`, `useNavTargetColor`, `ObjectIconTile` and `ObjectDefaultInspector`; all four exist in the tree at this head and read or write the key as the evidence line says. `Spec property liveness` is green.
- Claim flag 2, "the step that turns a blueprint into objects is not in this repository": ANSWERED, holds. No file under `packages/` or `ui/packages/` outside `packages/spec` reads a blueprint object's `icon` or builds an object from one; the lenient parse carries `color` through and the test builds an `ObjectSchema` body from it. The end-to-end acceptance line ("AI builds three objects, three colours") therefore cannot be closed in this repository and stays open on the card for PR 3 and the AI service; the claim says so and the line is a coordinator addition, not the maintainer's words.
- Claim flag 3, palette left to the dev: ANSWERED. The nine names are listed on the card in the claim comment, as the card asks, and the status names are kept out for a stated reason.
- Claim flag 4, branch name `claude/project-thread-4obpun` instead of `claude/issue-N-slug`: not a contract question; left to the seat, which recorded it as a platform exception.
- PR-body flag, `Skills-docs: follow-up` (PR 3): ACCEPTED for this head. No skill on `main` restates the object key list in a way the new key makes false; an additive key not yet taught is a gap, not a wrong statement. The card's "技能同步" line stays open until PR 3.
- PR-body flag, existing apps change from gray line icons to gray tiles in navigation: ANSWERED; it is the card's second acceptance line, limited here to navigation, the rest in PR 2.
- `open_questions`: none stated on the card or in the PR body.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; `useNavTargetColor` reads the object definition from the metadata cache the icon resolver already reads, by name.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Per `hits` file:

- `packages/spec/src/data/object-icon.ts`. Holds. One tuple, one type, one leaf; the leaf's describe lists the names from the tuple, so the docs and the refusal cannot drift from the enum. Against its first consumer: `ObjectIconTile` builds its palette set and its class map from `OBJECT_COLORS` (`Record` keyed by `ObjectColor`, so a tenth name fails type-check until it has a class), and falls back to `gray` for absent or unknown, which is what "Omit to draw the neutral gray" promises. Tried to break it: a stored hex from before the key existed cannot exist (the key was refused); a name from a newer spec draws gray instead of crashing; `gray` first in the tuple is pinned by test.
- `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`. Holds. One line beside `icon`, the shared leaf, no refinement and no default, so parse output for existing objects is unchanged.
- `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`. Holds. A named re-export of the tuple and the type only.
- `packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts`. Holds against the code it cites. The comment says the swatch row reads its names off the closed enum: `resolveRegisteredWidget` sends `color-picker` through `resolveColorWidgetKey`, which reads `schema.enum` and so lands on the swatch radiogroup, not the free hex input. A free value therefore cannot be typed in the generic form either.
- `packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts`. Holds. Lenient and strict both take the leaf by reference (identity pinned by test), in the two spellings of "optional" the file uses everywhere else; the rule text is shared by both sides, and the strict one adds only the null meaning. The rule states the card's item 6 (a colour on every object, different while the palette lasts).

Per implementing file:

- `object-icon-tile.tsx`: agrees. Name to class, static class strings, gray fallback, host glyph passthrough. `index.ts` exports match the changeset.
- `NavigationRenderer.tsx`: agrees with its own jsdoc and the claim's scope sentence. Only `type: 'object'` entries with an `objectName` take the tile; the glyph is the entry's own icon else the object's, the colour is always the object's; other entry types keep the line icon. The resolver is threaded through groups.
- `useNavTargetIcon.ts`, `UnifiedSidebar.tsx`, `nav-menu-renderer.tsx`: agree. Same read as the icon resolver; any non-palette string is narrowed to gray by the tile.
- `widgets.tsx`, `ObjectDefaultInspector.tsx`: agree. The swatches iterate `OBJECT_COLORS`; the colour half is on only when the host passes `onTileColorChange`, so every other picker host is unchanged; a colour is patched only on a click.
- `color-variant-field.tsx`: agrees. `gray` and `pink` are added to the CSS lookup only, spread first so no existing token changes value, and stay out of `COLOR_VARIANTS`.
- `object-schema-fls-references.ts`, `liveness/object.json`: agree, as in ① and ③.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract; accepted deviations unless noted):

- N1 (nit) — `OBJECT_COLOR_SCHEMA`'s describe, which is published on the reference pages, says "one object looks the same wherever its icon appears". At this head that is true in navigation and the designer only; list and record headers, search and chips still draw the line icon until PR 2 of this card. The liveness note states the limit correctly. Closed by PR 2 landing, no change needed here.
- N2 (nit) — the header of `object-icon.ts` still says the module is "outside the `data` barrel"; `index.ts` now re-exports two of its names. The leaves are still unexported, so the sentence is half stale, not wrong about what it protects. Follow-up wording.
- N3 (nit) — the changeset says the strict key is "required-but-nullable ... like `icon`" but drops the sentence its predecessors carry for hand producers ("a producer of the STRICT shape must now send `color` on each object, null when it has none"). Changeset prose is the lane seat's face; it can be added there without touching the reviewed files.
- N4 (nit) — neither picker can put a coloured object back to "no colour"; picking `gray` draws the same. And since `gray` is both a palette name and the unset neutral, the blueprint rule lets the model spend `gray` on an object, which then looks like an uncoloured one.
